# Replication: Adämmer and Weiß (2026)

This page reproduces **Table B.3** in the appendix of @adammer2026b. The table reports
simulated rejection rates of the seven Box-Ljung type ordinal pattern (BL-OP) tests with
$m = 3$ at level $\alpha = 0.05$, together with the classical Box-Ljung test on the sample
autocorrelations (BL-ACF), for maximal delays $w = 1, \ldots, 5$ and growing sample size
$T$.

## Libraries

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| message: false
using StatsOrdinalPatterns, Random, Statistics, Printf, DataFrames
import StatsOrdinalPatterns: init_dgp_op!
```

## Statistics of the paper and their types in the package

A BL-OP statistic aggregates one ordinal pattern statistic over the delays
$d = 1, \ldots, w$, weighting delay $d$ by its number of patterns $n_d = T - (m-1)d$.
[`stat_op_bp(data, w; chart_choice, m, ljung_box=true)`](../reference/stat_op_bp.qmd) computes it, and
[`crit_val_op_bp(w; chart_choice, m)`](../reference/crit_val_op_bp.qmd) returns the critical value. All tests reject for large
values.

| Table B.3 column | `chart_choice` | Summand for delay $d$ |
|:-----------------|:---------------|:----------------------|
| $\widehat{H}_{\text{BL}}$ | `Shannon(base=exp(1))` | $\tfrac{2}{6}\, n_d \big(\ln 6 - \widehat{H}^{(d)}\big)$ |
| $\widehat{H}^{\text{ex}}_{\text{BL}}$ | `ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1))` | $\tfrac{10}{6}\, n_d \big(5 \ln \tfrac{6}{5} - \widehat{H}_{\text{ex}}^{(d)}\big)$ |
| $\widehat{\Delta}^2_{\text{BL}}$ | [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](../reference/DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd) | $n_d\, \widehat{\Delta}^{2\,(d)}$ |
| $\widehat{\beta}_{\text{BL}}$ | [`UpDownBalance()`](../reference/UpDownBalance.qmd) | $n_d\, \big(\hat{\beta}^{(d)}\big)^2$ |
| $\widehat{\tau}_{\text{BL}}$ | [`Persistence()`](../reference/Persistence.qmd) | $n_d\, \big(\hat{\tau}^{(d)}\big)^2$ |
| $\widehat{\gamma}_{\text{BL}}$ | [`RotationalAsymmetry()`](../reference/RotationalAsymmetry.qmd) | $n_d\, \big(\hat{\gamma}^{(d)}\big)^2$ |
| $\widehat{\delta}_{\text{BL}}$ | [`UpDownScaling()`](../reference/UpDownScaling.qmd) | $n_d\, \big(\hat{\delta}^{(d)}\big)^2$ |
| $\widehat{\rho}_{\text{BL}}$ | [`stat_acf`](../reference/stat_acf.qmd) | $T(T+2)\, \hat{\rho}(d)^2 / (T - d)$ |

The critical value of $\widehat{\beta}_{\text{BL}}$ is a scaled $\chi^2(w)$ quantile. The
other six BL-OP statistics are correlated across delays, so `crit_val_op_bp` uses values
tabulated at $\alpha = 0.05$ for $w \le 5$. The BL-ACF statistic is compared with the
$\chi^2(w)$ quantile.

## Setup

The DGP is the Gaussian AR(1) process $X_t = 0.5\, X_{t-1} + \epsilon_t$ with
$\epsilon_t \sim \text{i.i.d. } N(0,1)$. The package type [`AR1`](../reference/AR1.qmd) describes it, and
`init_dgp_op!` fills a vector with a series started from the stationary distribution.

```{julia}
#| output: false
dgp = AR1(0.5, Normal(0, 1))
m = 3                                       # pattern length
level = 0.05                                # nominal significance level
ws = 1:5                                    # maximal delays of Table B.3
Ts = (100, 250, 500, 1000)                  # sample sizes of Table B.3
reps = 10_000                               # Monte Carlo replications

simulate!(x) = init_dgp_op!(dgp, x, dgp.dist, 1)

charts = [
    ("H", Shannon(base=exp(1))),
    ("Hex", ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1))),
    ("Δ²", DistanceToWhiteNoise()),
    ("β", UpDownBalance()),
    ("τ", Persistence()),
    ("γ", RotationalAsymmetry()),
    ("δ", UpDownScaling()),
]
```

## A single test

```{julia}
Random.seed!(1)
x = simulate!(zeros(500))
test_op_bp(x, 3; chart_choice=Persistence(), m=m, ljung_box=true)
```

## Running the power study

A loop over [`test_op_bp`](../reference/test_op_bp.qmd) would count the patterns of every delay again for each chart and
each $w$. Two observations avoid this:

* The BL-OP statistic for $w$ is the one for $w - 1$ plus the summand of delay $w$. One
  pass over $d = 1, \ldots, 5$ therefore yields the statistics for all five values of $w$.
* All seven summands of delay $d$ are functions of the same pattern frequencies
  $\hat{\mathbf{p}}^{(d)}$. [`stat_op`](../reference/stat_op.qmd) returns them, and [`chart_stat_op`](../reference/chart_stat_op.qmd) maps them to each
  statistic.

The critical values do not depend on the data, so they are taken once per $T$. Every
replication draws one series and tests it for all charts and all $w$.

```{julia}
#| output: false
# summand of delay d, as in the table above, without the weight n_d
bl_term(::Shannon, s) = (log(6) - s) / 3
bl_term(::ShannonExtropy, s) = 5 / 3 * (5 * log(6 / 5) - s)
bl_term(::DistanceToWhiteNoise, s) = s
bl_term(_, s) = s^2

function power(T, reps)
    crits = [crit_val_op_bp(w; chart_choice=cc, m=m) for (_, cc) in charts, w in ws]
    crits_acf = [quantile(Chisq(w), 1 - level) for w in ws]

    tasks = map(Iterators.partition(1:reps, cld(reps, Threads.nthreads()))) do idx
        Threads.@spawn begin
            x = Vector{Float64}(undef, T)
            bl = zeros(length(charts))
            hits = zeros(Int, length(charts) + 1, length(ws))
            for _ in idx
                simulate!(x)
                fill!(bl, 0.0)
                q = 0.0
                for d in ws
                    n = T - (m - 1) * d
                    p̂ = stat_op(x; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)), m=m, d=d)[2]
                    for (j, (_, cc)) in enumerate(charts)
                        bl[j] += n * bl_term(cc, chart_stat_op(p̂, cc))
                        hits[j, d] += bl[j] > crits[j, d]
                    end
                    q += T * (T + 2) * stat_acf(x, d)^2 / (T - d)
                    hits[end, d] += q > crits_acf[d]
                end
            end
            hits
        end
    end
    return sum(fetch.(tasks)) ./ reps
end
```

The shortcut has to give the same statistic as `stat_op_bp`, not merely a similar one:

```{julia}
let T = 400, x = simulate!(zeros(T))
    ok = all(
        begin
            s = sum((T - (m - 1) * d) *
                    bl_term(cc, chart_stat_op(stat_op(x; chart_choice=cc, m=m, d=d)[2], cc))
                    for d in 1:w)
            s ≈ stat_op_bp(x, w; chart_choice=cc, m=m, ljung_box=true)
        end for (_, cc) in charts, w in ws
    )
    (shortcut_matches_stat_op_bp=ok,)
end
```

::: {.callout-note}
With `reps = 10_000` the whole table takes about a second on a multi core machine, and the
standard error of a rejection rate is at most $\sqrt{0.25 / 10^4} = 0.005$.
:::

## Table B.3: AR(1) with $\alpha_1 = 0.5$

```{julia}
#| output: false
Random.seed!(2026)
res = Dict(T => power(T, reps) for T in Ts)
names = vcat([n for (n, _) in charts], "ACF")
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
tab = DataFrame(w=Int[], T=Int[])
for nm in names
    tab[!, nm] = Float64[]
end
for w in ws, T in Ts
    push!(tab, vcat(w, T, round.(res[T][:, w], digits=3)))
end
tab
```

```{julia}
cmp = DataFrame(w=Int[], T=Int[], statistic=String[], paper=Float64[],
    replicated=Float64[], dev=Float64[])
for w in ws, T in Ts, (j, nm) in enumerate(names)
    r = round(res[T][j, w], digits=3)
    push!(cmp, (w, T, nm, published[(w, T)][j], r, round(r - published[(w, T)][j], digits=3)))
end
cmp
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
@printf("largest absolute deviation: %.3f\n", maximum(abs, cmp.dev))
@printf("mean absolute deviation:    %.3f\n", mean(abs, cmp.dev))
@printf("Monte Carlo standard error: at most %.3f\n", sqrt(0.25 / reps))
```

All 160 entries are reproduced within two Monte Carlo standard errors.
